-- A scheduled eval run (evals/scheduled.py posts {source: 'eval', kind: 'run', data: run}).
insert into eval_run (set_name, passed, total, failed_ids, seconds, results_path)
select d->>'set_name', (d->>'passed')::int, (d->>'total')::int,
       array(select jsonb_array_elements_text(case when jsonb_typeof(d->'failed_ids') = 'array' then d->'failed_ids' else '[]'::jsonb end)),
       (d->>'seconds')::numeric, d->>'results_path'
from (select $1::jsonb as d) r
returning id, at, set_name, passed, total

-- One row per incident; the throttle state is this table (design part 1): at most one Telegram message per
-- (source, workflow, node, kind) per 30 minutes.
-- 1) Same-key incidents take turns. Without this, simultaneous error runs (2 workers x 10 executions) all see "nothing
--    alerted yet" and all alert. n8n's Postgres node ("single" batching) sends both statements as ONE query, which
--    Postgres runs as one transaction, so the lock holds until it commits. This statement returns no row (n8n would
--    output it as an item).
select 1 where pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext(concat_ws('|', $1::text, nullif($2, ''), nullif($3, ''), $4::text)))::text = 'locked';
-- 2) The row is its own claim: notified_at = now() when no row of the key was alerted in the last 30 minutes (never for
--    kind ok); "Release claim" clears it again if the Telegram send fails. This statement starts after the lock, so it
--    sees a claim the previous holder committed. suppressed = rows of the key in the window that were not alerted (the
--    "+N more"); like the claim check, it reads the table as it was before this insert.
with ins as (
  insert into incident_log (source, workflow, node, kind, message, execution_id, ref, data, notified_at)
  select $1, nullif($2, ''), nullif($3, ''), $4, nullif($5, ''), nullif($6, ''), nullif($7, ''), nullif($8, 'null')::jsonb,
         case when $4::text is distinct from 'ok' and not exists (
                select 1 from incident_log l
                 where l.source = $1 and l.workflow is not distinct from nullif($2, '') and l.node is not distinct from nullif($3, '')
                   and l.kind is not distinct from $4::text and l.notified_at > now() - interval '30 minutes')
              then now() end
  returning *
)
select ins.id, ins.at, ins.source, ins.workflow, ins.node, ins.kind, ins.message, ins.execution_id, ins.ref,
       ins.data->>'workflow_id' as workflow_id, ins.notified_at is not null as claimed,
       (select count(*) from incident_log l
         where l.source = ins.source and l.workflow is not distinct from ins.workflow
           and l.node is not distinct from ins.node and l.kind is not distinct from ins.kind
           and l.at > now() - interval '30 minutes' and l.notified_at is null) as suppressed
from ins

-- The Telegram send failed: give the claim back, so the next incident of this key alerts instead of being counted.
update incident_log set notified_at = null where id = $1 returning id, notified_at

parameters.content:
## Error reporter (incidents -> Telegram)
**Error Trigger:** every RAG workflow sets *Error workflow* to this one, so each failed execution lands here. **Incident webhook** `POST /webhook/rag-incident` (same bearer token as /rag-chat): the pipe, backups, evals, the watchdog and in-workflow error branches post `{source, kind, message, ref?, workflow?, workflow_id?, node?, execution_id?, data?}`.
One `incident_log` row each (Supabase). **Throttle:** at most one Telegram message per (source, workflow, node, kind) per 30 min: the first row of a key claims the alert (under a per-key lock), later ones are counted ("+N more"); a failed send releases the claim. Kind `ok` is recorded, never sent. Eval runs go to `eval_run`.
**Text hygiene:** message, workflow and node are cut at `chatInput` / `messages` / `content` (any case), the message capped at 300 characters, data at 4,000: no question text ever reaches Telegram. If this workflow fails itself, n8n runs it once as its own error workflow (no loop).
